newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - PORSCHE PROFIT UP, PLANS OUTPUT IN FINLAND.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - PORSCHE PROFIT UP, PLANS OUTPUT IN FINLAND.

text.p: German sports car maker Porsche AG said on Friday its profit more than trebled in the first half of 1996/1997 and that it would build cars at Valmet in Finland to meet strong demand for its new Boxster car.

Group profit surged to 36 million marks ($22 million) in the six months to January 31 compared with 10.3 million marks in the year-earlier period, while group sales jumped 20 percent to 1.7 billion marks, Dr.Ing.h.c.F. Porsche said in a statement.
Unit sales rose 25 percent to 12,800 units, of which 3,150 were Boxsters, Porsche's first new car in almost two decades.

Porsche said demand for the two-seat cabriolet was so strong that it planned to crank up production, building 5,000 Boxsters per year at Valmet Automotive in Uusikaupunkl, Finland, from the autumn of 1997.
The announcement confirmed media reports in Germany and Finland this week. Customers reportedly have to wait more than a year for delivery of a Boxster.
Shares in Porsche surged more than four percent on the earnings news in pre-bourse trade. They climbed to 1,450 marks, outpacing the broader market.
Porsche said it had reached the limit of its production capacity at its German assembly plant in Zuffenhausen and did not want to increase fixed costs.

But it stressed that it remained commited to maintaining jobs at its German plant and that the production at Valmet would create about 1,000 jobs at components suppliers in Germany, which account for about four fifths of Boxster production.

"Porsche will continue to keep capacity utilisation consistantly high in Zuffenhausen and thereby secure employment," Porsche said in the statement which was released ahead of its annual general meeting in Stuttgart.

Porsche said it had chosen Valmet because of its good reputation. It plans to dispatch experienced Porsche workers to Valmet to ensure that the cars assembled there leave the plant with the "customary high Porsche quality."
"Scandinavia is held in high regard worldwide as a production site and Valmet has an extremely good reputation as a carmaker," Porsche said.
